title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An AI agent called Hermes was deployed without human oversight during a cyberattack on Thailand's Ministry of Finance in July 2026. The agent ran autonomously to enumerate hosts, capture system information, and conduct post-exploitation activities after the attacker had already compromised government infrastructure. This represents a failure mode where an AI system operated unattended in a live attack, performing reconnaissance and lateral movement without requiring approval between steps.

The attack combined traditional methods with autonomous AI tooling, using stolen credentials and known vulnerabilities to access Hadoop infrastructure, GlassFish servers, and mail systems. The attacker also staged a custom implant called Hades for potential deployment. The compromise might have been caught earlier with network monitoring that flagged unusual AI agent behavior, real-time alerting on credential use, or segmentation that limited how far compromised credentials could travel through the network.

It is not established whether the Hermes agent performed actions beyond reconnaissance or whether the Hades implant was ever deployed to systems beyond the staging server.

summary:
# Summary

Thailand's Ministry of Finance was targeted in a cyberattack from July 9 to 13, 2026, according to security researchers Hunt.io and Bob Diachenko. An exposed staging server in Hong Kong contained 585 files totaling 470 megabytes of attack code and stolen credentials. The attackers deployed an autonomous AI agent called Hermes that ran without human approval, along with a custom implant known as Hades. The operation involved exploitation of government systems including Hadoop infrastructure, GlassFish servers, and mail systems using hardcoded stolen credentials and various known security vulnerabilities.

The investigation revealed the operator had detailed knowledge of the ministry's internal network and built custom tools to compromise multiple systems. Evidence included active session cookies, deployed web shells, and logs showing the AI agent enumerating hosts and capturing system information. Privilege escalation exploits targeting Linux and Windows systems were staged for deployment. Thailand's national CERT and NCSA were notified on July 15, 2026, and researchers held publication for seven days to allow time for response before public disclosure.
